# Windows `.cmd` shims for graph-manager's terminals

## What to build

graph-manager (`apps/graph-manager`) puts two commands on the `PATH` of its terminals by writing shell scripts into `<dataDir>/bin`: `graph-execution` (the engine, or graph-manager's `shim.js` that handles `--sandbox`) and `graph-manager-mcp` (the MCP server that gives agents graph-manager's tools). Both are POSIX `#!/bin/sh` scripts and both writers return `false` on `win32`, so a Windows terminal has neither command. This slice makes `writeGraphExecutionShim` and `writeMcpShim` write `graph-execution.cmd` and `graph-manager-mcp.cmd` on Windows, fixes the `PATH` handling that this switches on there, and makes the agent configurations name `graph-manager-mcp.cmd` on Windows. Everything is selected by an optional `platform` parameter (default `process.platform`) so the tests run on Linux, macOS and Windows CI. The POSIX output stays byte-for-byte unchanged.

Scope limits (other tasks run in parallel):

- Edit only `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts`, `agents.ts`, `terminals.test.ts`, `agents.test.ts`.
- Do **not** edit `config.ts`, `main.ts`, `docker.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `sandbox-run.ts`, `sandbox-tools.ts`. None is needed.
- `app.ts` needs **no** change: its calls (lines 86–93) use the default platform. Leave it alone, including the comment.
- Do **not** edit any README or `docs/wiki` page. `apps/graph-manager/README.md` line 305 and `docs/wiki/features/agent-tools.md` line 36 say the shim is not written on Windows; a later documentation task removes them.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts`
  - lines 115–119 `defaultShell`: Windows terminals are `powershell.exe`, which finds `.cmd` files on `PATH` through `PATHEXT`.
  - lines 125–138 `terminalEnv`: line 136 prepends `binDir` to `env.PATH`. You change it.
  - lines 140–165 `writeGraphExecutionShim`, `writeMcpShim`: you change them.
  - lines 49–59 `TerminalManagerOptions`, lines 180–183 the constructor: you add `platform`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/app.ts` lines 83–96 — read only. `hasShim || hasMcp ? binDir : undefined` is the only thing the two booleans gate: whether `binDir` goes on the terminals' `PATH`. On Windows both are `false` today, so the `PATH` code never ran there.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/shim.ts` lines 92–110 — read only. `shim.js` reads `GM_ENGINE_BIN` and runs `node <bin> <args>`, or posts to graph-manager for `--sandbox`. Without the variable it prints `error: GM_ENGINE_BIN is not set` and exits 2.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/agents.ts`
  - lines 16–19 `MCP_NAME`, `MCP_COMMAND = "graph-manager-mcp"`.
  - lines 35–42 `AgentAdapter`, lines 49–95 `QWEN_ENTRY` and `AGENTS`, lines 158–166 `writeClaudeMcpConfig`: you change these.
  - lines 101–111 `commandLine(argv, platform)` and lines 121–151 `findOnPath(…, platform, …)`: the existing injected-platform pattern, and the case-insensitive env lookup at lines 130–132.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` line 67 (`adapter.launch({ dataDir: config.dataDir })`) — read only; it keeps working through the default.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.test.ts` lines 1–33, 123–147, 266–280 and `agents.test.ts` lines 1–73: the tests you extend.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/test-helpers.ts` lines 9–14: `tempDir()`.

## Patterns to follow

**Injected platform** (`agents.ts:104`): an optional last parameter, never `process.platform` inside the body.

```ts
export function commandLine(argv: string[], platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform): string {
  if (platform === "win32") {
```

**Case-insensitive env names on Windows** (`agents.ts:130`):

```ts
// Windows env names are case-insensitive, and `Path` is the usual spelling there.
const get = (name: string): string | undefined =>
  win ? Object.entries(env).find(([k]) => k.toUpperCase() === name)?.[1] : env[name];
```

**The POSIX shims today** (`terminals.ts:148–152`, `162`). These strings must not change:

```ts
`#!/bin/sh\nGM_ENGINE_BIN=${JSON.stringify(bin)} exec node ${JSON.stringify(shimJs)} "$@"\n`
`#!/bin/sh\nexec node ${JSON.stringify(bin)} "$@"\n`
`#!/bin/sh\nexec node ${JSON.stringify(mcpJs)} "$@"\n`
```

**The `.cmd` files** (exact content, every line ends with `\r\n`, paths written verbatim, no `JSON.stringify`):

```bat
@echo off
setlocal
set "GM_ENGINE_BIN=C:\ge\dist\cli.js"
node "C:\gm\dist\server\shim.js" %*
exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
```

```bat
@echo off
node "C:\ge\dist\cli.js" %*
exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
```

- First block: `graph-execution.cmd` when `shimJs` exists. Second block: `graph-execution.cmd` without `shimJs`, and `graph-manager-mcp.cmd` with `mcpJs` in place of the path.
- `@echo off`: the commands are not echoed into the terminal (or into the MCP server's stdout, which carries JSON-RPC).
- `set "VAR=value"`: the quotes around the whole assignment keep spaces and `&` in the path literal and add no trailing space to the value.
- `setlocal`: in an interactive `cmd.exe` a batch file runs inside the session, so without it `GM_ENGINE_BIN` would stay set in the user's shell.
- `%*`: all arguments, as typed.
- `exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%`: the command's exit code is node's (the shim's `2`, a failed run's code).
- `%` in a path would be expanded by `cmd.exe` and `"` would end the quoting, so a path with either cannot be written safely: return `false` and write nothing. Also reject `\r` and `\n`. Test: `/[%"\r\n]/`.
- On `win32` only the `.cmd` file is written, not the extensionless POSIX script.
- Known limits, do not try to solve: `cmd.exe` asks `Terminate batch job (Y/N)?` after Ctrl+C, and reads the file in the console's code page, so a non-ASCII path can fail. Do not add `chcp`.

**Which name each agent gets on Windows.** A program started without a shell does not get `PATHEXT` resolution: Node's `spawn("graph-manager-mcp")` and Rust's `Command` look for that exact name (or `.exe`) and never find `graph-manager-mcp.cmd`. So:

| Consumer | Where the name is | `win32` | Other platforms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `<dataDir>/agents/claude-mcp.json`, `command` | `graph-manager-mcp.cmd` | `graph-manager-mcp` |
| Codex | argv `-c mcp_servers.graph-manager.command="…"` | `graph-manager-mcp.cmd` | `graph-manager-mcp` |
| OpenCode | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, `mcp.graph-manager.command[0]` | `graph-manager-mcp.cmd` | `graph-manager-mcp` |
| Qwen Code | `.qwen/settings.json`, committed in the workspace | `graph-manager-mcp` (unchanged) | `graph-manager-mcp` |

Qwen's entry stays the bare name on every platform: the file is committed and shared between machines, a `.cmd` name would break it on Linux and macOS, and `matches` compares it with `isDeepStrictEqual`. Say this in a comment at `QWEN_ENTRY`. The name stays a bare file name found on `PATH`, never an absolute path.

**Test pattern** (`terminals.test.ts:266–272`):

```ts
const t = await tempDir();
cleanup = t.cleanup;
const js = path.join(t.dir, "mcp.js");
await writeFile(js, "");
expect(writeMcpShim(path.join(t.dir, "bin"), js)).toBe(true);
```

The existing `describe.skipIf(skip)` blocks are skipped on Windows because they use `/bin/sh`. Put the new tests in **new top-level `describe` blocks without `skipIf`**, so they run on all three CI systems (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`: ubuntu, macos, windows; it runs `npm ci`, typecheck, lint, test and does not build `dist`).

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** `writeGraphExecutionShim(binDir: string, bin: string, shimJs?: string, platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform): boolean`:
  - `const p = platform === "win32" ? path.win32 : path.posix;` and replace the guard with `if (!p.isAbsolute(bin) || !bin.endsWith(".js")) return false;`.
  - `const useShim = shimJs !== undefined && existsSync(shimJs);`
  - Not `win32`: the existing code, unchanged (file `graph-execution`, mode `0o755`, `chmodSync`).
  - `win32`: return `false` when `bin`, or `shimJs` when `useShim`, matches `/[%"\r\n]/`. Otherwise `mkdirSync(binDir, { recursive: true })`, write `path.join(binDir, "graph-execution.cmd")` with the content above, return `true`. No `chmodSync`.
- **IMPLEMENT** `writeMcpShim(binDir: string, mcpJs: string, platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform): boolean`: `false` when `mcpJs` does not exist (all platforms, as today); on `win32`, `false` for `/[%"\r\n]/`, otherwise write `graph-manager-mcp.cmd`; elsewhere unchanged.
- **IMPLEMENT** a small private helper for the two `.cmd` bodies, for example `cmdShim(js: string, engineBin?: string): string` that joins the lines with `\r\n` and ends with `\r\n`.
- **IMPLEMENT** `terminalEnv(base, binDir?, reviewersFile?, platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform)`. Replace line 136 with:

```ts
if (binDir) {
  const win = platform === "win32";
  // Windows env names are case-insensitive and `Path` is the usual spelling: a second `PATH` key would hide it.
  const key = (win ? Object.keys(env).find((k) => k.toUpperCase() === "PATH") : undefined) ?? "PATH";
  const delimiter = win ? path.win32.delimiter : path.posix.delimiter;
  env[key] = env[key] ? `${binDir}${delimiter}${env[key]}` : binDir;
}
```

- **IMPLEMENT** `platform?: NodeJS.Platform` in `TerminalManagerOptions`, passed by the constructor as the fourth argument of `terminalEnv`.
- **IMPLEMENT** update the two doc comments (lines 140–143, 157): on Windows the file is `<name>.cmd`; `false` for a path with `%`, `"` or a line break.
- **GOTCHA**:
  - Use native `path.join` for the file you write (`binDir` is a real folder of the host); use `p` only for `isAbsolute(bin)`. That keeps `platform: "win32"` testable on Linux, where `path.win32.isAbsolute` accepts both `C:\x\cli.js` and `/tmp/x/cli.js`.
  - Do not check that `bin` exists (today's behaviour).
  - This is the reason `terminalEnv` must change in this task: once a shim is written on Windows, `binDir` is set, and `env.PATH = binDir` next to the inherited `Path` would leave the terminal without `node`.
  - Leave `defaultShell` and line 337 as they are.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck -w graph-manager`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/agents.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** `export function mcpCommand(platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform): string` returning `` `${MCP_COMMAND}.cmd` `` on `win32` and `MCP_COMMAND` otherwise. Keep `MCP_COMMAND` exported and unchanged.
- **IMPLEMENT** `AgentAdapter.launch(o: { dataDir: string; platform?: NodeJS.Platform }): AgentLaunch`. Codex: `` `mcp_servers.${MCP_NAME}.command="${mcpCommand(platform)}"` ``. OpenCode: `command: [mcpCommand(platform)]`. Claude and Qwen ignore `platform`.
- **IMPLEMENT** `writeClaudeMcpConfig(dataDir: string, platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform): string` with `command: mcpCommand(platform)`.
- **IMPLEMENT** the comment at `QWEN_ENTRY` (see the table), and update the comment at line 18.
- **GOTCHA**: `claudeMcpConfigPath`, `commandLine`, `findOnPath`, `prepareProjectConfig` and `projectConfig.matches` are unchanged. Callers in `app.ts:90` and `routes/terminals.ts:67` pass no platform and need no edit.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck -w graph-manager`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.test.ts`

Add `import { execa } from "execa";` (already a dependency). New top-level blocks:

- `describe("Windows .cmd shims", …)` with `"win32"` passed explicitly; each test uses `tempDir()` and sets `cleanup`.
  - Shim form: `cli = "C:\\Program Files\\ge\\dist\\cli.js"`, `shimJs = path.join(dir, "shim.js")` (written, empty). `writeGraphExecutionShim(bin, cli, shimJs, "win32")` is `true` and `graph-execution.cmd` equals exactly `` `@echo off\r\nsetlocal\r\nset "GM_ENGINE_BIN=${cli}"\r\nnode "${shimJs}" %*\r\nexit /b %ERRORLEVEL%\r\n` ``. No file named `graph-execution` exists in that folder.
  - Direct form (missing `shimJs`, and `shimJs` undefined): exactly `` `@echo off\r\nnode "${cli}" %*\r\nexit /b %ERRORLEVEL%\r\n` ``.
  - `false` and no file for: `bin` `"graph-execution"`; `"C:\\ge\\cli.mjs"`; `"C:\\100%\\cli.js"`; `'C:\\a"b\\cli.js'`; and a `shimJs` that exists in a folder named `50%`.
  - `writeMcpShim(bin, js, "win32")`: exact content with `js`; `false` for a missing file and for a file in a folder named `50%`.
  - The content has no `\n` that is not preceded by `\r`.
- `describe("terminalEnv PATH", …)`:
  - `terminalEnv({ Path: "C:\\Windows" }, "C:\\d\\bin", undefined, "win32")` has `Path` `"C:\\d\\bin;C:\\Windows"` and no `PATH` key.
  - `terminalEnv({}, "C:\\d\\bin", undefined, "win32").PATH` is `"C:\\d\\bin"`.
  - `terminalEnv({ PATH: "/usr/bin" }, "/d/bin", undefined, "linux").PATH` is `"/d/bin:/usr/bin"`.
- POSIX unchanged, in the existing skipped-on-Windows block: add `expect(writeMcpShim(...))` content equals exactly `` `#!/bin/sh\nexec node ${JSON.stringify(js)} "$@"\n` ``. Keep the assertions at lines 141–146 as they are.
- `describe.runIf(process.platform === "win32")("the .cmd shims run", …)`, a real execution on Windows CI with stand-in scripts (no built engine needed). Use a bin folder with a space, `path.join(dir, "my bin")`:
  - `cli.js`: `console.log('engine', process.argv.slice(2).join(' ')); process.exit(process.argv.includes('--fail') ? 7 : 0)`.
  - Direct form: `await execa(path.join(bin, "graph-execution.cmd"), ["--version"], { reject: false })` has `exitCode` 0 and stdout containing `engine --version`; with `["--fail"]` the `exitCode` is 7.
  - Shim form with a stand-in `shim.js` (`console.log('shim', process.env.GM_ENGINE_BIN, process.argv.slice(2).join(' '))`): stdout contains `` `shim ${cli} --version` ``.
  - `graph-manager-mcp.cmd` with a stand-in `mcp.js` that prints one line: stdout is exactly that line (nothing echoed).
  - Found by name: `execa("graph-execution", ["--version"], { env: terminalEnv(process.env, bin), extendEnv: false, reject: false })` exits 0.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/agents.test.ts`

- Lines 27–51 run on Windows CI too and would now see `.cmd` there. Pass `platform: "linux"` to `launch` and `"linux"` to `writeClaudeMcpConfig` in the existing assertions.
- Add: with `platform: "win32"`, Codex's argv is `["codex", "-c", 'mcp_servers.graph-manager.command="graph-manager-mcp.cmd"']`, OpenCode's `command` is `["graph-manager-mcp.cmd"]`, `writeClaudeMcpConfig(dir, "win32")` writes `command: "graph-manager-mcp.cmd"`, `mcpCommand("win32")` / `mcpCommand("darwin")` give the two names, and Qwen's `projectConfig.apply({})` still has `command: "graph-manager-mcp"`.
- Do not change `routes/agents.test.ts` (skipped on Windows; it asserts the bare name on POSIX and must keep passing).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `platform` `"win32"`, `writeGraphExecutionShim` writes `<binDir>/graph-execution.cmd` with exactly the content above (both forms) and returns `true`; `writeMcpShim` does the same for `graph-manager-mcp.cmd`.
- [ ] Both return `false` and write nothing for a path containing `%`, `"` or a line break; `writeGraphExecutionShim` still returns `false` for a non-absolute or non-`.js` `bin`, and `writeMcpShim` for a missing `mcpJs`.
- [ ] Every line of a `.cmd` file ends with `\r\n`.
- [ ] On Linux and macOS the files written are byte-for-byte what they were; the existing tests pass unmodified apart from the pinned platform in `agents.test.ts`.
- [ ] On Windows the terminal's environment has one path variable, with `<binDir>;` in front of the inherited value.
- [ ] On `win32` Claude Code's config, Codex's argv and OpenCode's config name `graph-manager-mcp.cmd`; Qwen's committed entry and every non-Windows value stay `graph-manager-mcp`.
- [ ] On Windows CI the written `.cmd` files run: arguments reach node, `GM_ENGINE_BIN` reaches `shim.js`, exit code 7 comes back as 7.
- [ ] No file other than the four named above is changed.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass at the repository root, apart from the known environment failure below.

## Validation commands

```bash
# from apps/graph-manager
npx vitest run src/server/terminals.test.ts
npx vitest run src/server/agents.test.ts src/server/routes/agents.test.ts src/server/routes/terminals.test.ts

# from the repository root
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
git status --short   # only terminals.ts, agents.ts and their two test files
```

Known environment failure, not caused by this task: `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` "exits 2 at startup when --provider claude is not on the PATH" fails wherever a real `claude` is installed next to `node`. The `describe.runIf(win32)` tests are skipped on Linux; Windows CI runs them.
